evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 告: glyph records, Shuowen, reconstruction analysis, cited uses
evidence.text: The entry displays one oracle-bone example, 22 of 91 bronze examples, and one small-seal example. It reports Zhang Yujin’s proposal that 告 derives from 舌 by extending 舌’s central stroke upward, depicting an open mouth with tongue and relating to speaking/telling. It gives a 牛+口 sacrificial interpretation as an alternative. The entry cites oracle-bone 合集1166甲 for a sacrificial use read 祰, 屯南997 for reporting a deer, bronze inscriptions for reporting, admonishing, and accusation, and a Guodian slip for telling. These reports do not establish a linear chronology of meanings.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 舌: graph analysis and modern reading display
evidence.text: The 舌 entry describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as depicting a tongue, and describes the oracle-bone graph as showing a tongue projecting from a mouth. This is relevant evidence for the proposed relationship between 舌 and 告, but does not independently prove that 告 developed from 舌. CUHK displays Mandarin for 舌 as an image-rendered reading that was not recoverable as text in the inspected page.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00528-001 吿: form history and cited Shuowen analysis
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen’s explanation that an ox striking a person, with its horns restrained by a crossbar, informs people, analyzing 告 as 口 plus 牛. It says the seal form was abbreviated in clerical transformation and regularized into the modern form. This is a transmitted lexicographic and graphic account, not independent verification of the interpretation of Shang forms.
evidence.title: [A00528] 告 - 教育部《異體字字典》

search_audit.outcome: Searches yielded general Unihan documentation but not character-specific records. Direct Unihan record URLs, Commons file page and Commons imageinfo API attempts were inaccessible. No file provenance or licensing was verified.

gaps: The upper element of the early graph remains disputed. The inspected sources present the historical Shuowen 牛+口 explanation and a later 舌-derived analysis; the dossier also reports Chen Meilan’s abbreviated 壴+口 proposal from an abstract. No inspected source settles the alternatives.

CUHK lists oracle-bone, bronze and small-seal records, but its linked oracle image opened as an empty page in this browser. The graph pixels were not visually inspected, so no independent visual comparison or corruption analysis is made.

The cited Shang examples are reported by the CUHK database as 合集1166甲 and 屯南997; their specific artifact dates and inscription images were not independently checked. The listed sacrificial, reporting, admonishing, accusatory and telling uses do not by themselves establish semantic chronology or the link between sacrificial and reporting uses.

The exact Unicode Unihan click-through records for 告 and 口 were inaccessible despite direct attempts and searches. The packet’s exact local kMandarin rows are reported as local data, not external confirmation.

No proposed graphic component is securely established as phonetic. Therefore no component-versus-host historical sound comparison is warranted. Local Baxter–Sagart rows are preserved as dataset readings only.

The Commons file page for 告-seal.svg, the page for Shuowen Seal Radical 021.svg, and exact-title API metadata requests were inaccessible. The provided manifest leads do not verify pixels, source attribution, licensing, or whether a redraw is useful; no glyph asset should be selected on this evidence.
The full text of Chen Meilan’s article was not opened in this invocation; the proposal is available only from the dossier’s prior abstract evidence, not freshly verified here.

The dossier’s proposed regional whole-graph use from 校 and Thai cognacy were outside the inspected primary evidence in this invocation and remain unresolved; neither is treated as graphic formation evidence.
